issues.title: Hy's Law flags threshold the stored ULN ratio rather than the value against ULN

issues.title: AVAL rules for the Hy's Law parameters cannot be checked as written
issues.summary: The citable AVAL section gives only precision. Per the adjudicator, the native HYLAW value rule refers to parameter BILHY, which is not in the PARAMCD codelist, so the combined rule does not resolve.
issues.expected: SAP page 12: a flag for the modified Hy's Law assessment from bilirubin and ALT/AST above 1.5 x ULN; ALT, AST and BILI keep their ADLBC values.
issues.observed: Not probed. Pilot 6's adlbhy.r sets BILIHY from R2A1HI > 1.5 (L79-L88), TRANSHY per sample date (L91-L104) and HYLAW when both hold on one date (L107-L134).
issues.action: Correct the HYLAW value-level rule to name an existing parameter or the source ratios, and expose the value-level rules so AVAL can be probed.

citations.quote:
An abnormal flag will be assigned to indicate whether a subject
meets the criteria for a modified Hy’s Law assessment of liver function, defined as:
1.            Transaminase (SGPT/ALT or SGOT/AST) elevations (i.e., >1.5*ULN) and
2.            Bilirubin elevated to greater than 1.5*ULN.

Codelist PARAMCD_ADLBHY: ALT = Alanine Aminotransferase (U/L); AST = Aspartate Aminotransferase (U/L); BILI = Bilirubin (umol/L); BILIHY = Bilirubin 1.5 x ULN; TRANSHY = Transaminase 1.5 x ULN; HYLAW = Total Bili 1.5 x ULN and Transaminase 1.5 x ULN

mutate(has_elevated = if_else(R2A1HI > 1.5, 1, 0)) %>%
arrange(STUDYID, USUBJID, VISIT, VISITNUM, ADT, desc(has_elevated)) %>%
distinct(STUDYID, USUBJID, VISIT, VISITNUM, ADT, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
mutate(
PARAMCD = "TRANSHY",
PARAM = "Transaminase 1.5 x ULN",
PARAMN = 5,
AVAL = has_elevated,

has_bili = any(PARAMCD == "BILI" & R2A1HI > 1.5, na.rm = TRUE),
has_trans = any(PARAMCD %in% c("ALT", "AST") & R2A1HI > 1.5, na.rm = TRUE),
.groups = "drop"
) %>%
mutate(
PARAMCD = "HYLAW",
PARAM = "Total Bili 1.5 x ULN and Transaminase 1.5 x ULN",
PARAMN = 6,
AVAL = if_else(has_bili & has_trans, 1, 0),

issues.title: Lab analysis visits are inherited from ADLBC, not assigned by SAP date windows
issues.summary: The SAP assigns laboratory assessments to visits by actual-date windows; the specification copies ADLBC.AVISIT, and no retained table gives laboratory window bounds.
issues.expected: SAP page 11: labs are assigned by actual date (day = visit date - randomization date), closest to target, earlier one on ties, retrieval visits included for Week 24.
issues.observed: The specification copies ADLBC.AVISIT (collected-visit labels, retrieval visits excluded upstream). Pilot 6's adlbhy.r keeps Baseline to Week 24 visits (L48-L54). Not probed.
issues.action: Decide whether laboratory visits follow the SAP window algorithm; if so, document laboratory window bounds and implement them, otherwise amend the SAP.

Actual visit days will be determined relative to the date of randomization, using the algorithm {day = visit date – randomization date}.
If multiple assessments fall into the same visit window (windows defined in following table), then the assessment closest to the target day will be selected.
[Note that retrieval visits (visit number 201) are included for the purpose of selecting assessments for the week 24 visit window.]
If two assessments are equidistant from the target day, then the assessment prior to the target day will be selected.
Hematology, and clinical chemistry will be summarized for Baseline and Weeks 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, and 26 (Visits 1, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, and 13, respectively).
